result.title: SpikWM: Efficient End-to-End Spiking World Modeling for Visual Planning
result.summary: Goal-conditioned planning with image observations and goals requires predictions that distinguish visual states and action consequences. Spiking neural networks offer sparse computation, but single-step spikes can obscure motion cues and merge actions with different physical outcomes. We propose the Spiking Latent World Model (SpikWM), an end-to-end joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) with one simulation step per image and one neural update per latent position. Spiking Regional Encoding retains spatial cues through regional pooling. Bi-Spike Action Encoding combines positive and negative binary responses, while Causal Membrane Prediction carries subthreshold evidence across the latent history with learned group-wise time constants. The encoder and predictor are trained jointly on reward-free image--action trajectories using next-embedding prediction and SIGReg. With a common planner, SpikWM achieves mean success rates of $88.67\%$, $97.33\%$, $99.33\%$, and $86.67\%$ on Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, and OGBench-Cube, respectively, outperforming two spiking baselines. Push-T ablations support each module, and controlled replays examine responses to appearance and physical state changes. Under a matched planning budget, SpikWM reduces estimated arithmetic energy by $75.6\%$ relative to LeWM. Code will be released at https://github.com/ShawnYE618/SpikWM.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SpikWM：一个端到端的脉冲神经网络 JEPA 世界模型，通过区域池化保留空间线索、双脉冲动作编码区分正负响应，并用带可学习时间常数的膜电位预测在 latent 历史间传递阈下证据，在无奖励的图像—动作轨迹上联合训练编码器与预测器，用于目标条件视觉规划。
AI.relevance_reason: 其动作条件的 latent 状态转移与跨历史膜电位累积可能为 LVR 的循环状态更新与 latent 轨迹训练提供线索，稀疏脉冲计算与能耗估算也可供核查「THINK/STOP」的计算成本维度；但工作面向世界模型规划，未涉及 VLM 推理的视觉证据筛选与停止决策，需较多核查。
